text:
ConocoPhillips climbed 2.67% today to $154.03, capping a five-day rally that's added 5.13% over two weeks. The immediate catalyst is the sharp rise in crude oil prices — US oil jumped to $103.37 a barrel, with global oil hitting $123.10, driven by geopolitical tension in the Middle East as Iranian attacks on shipping have intensified. For an integrated oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly boost earnings, which is why the stock has been rising steadily since late October.

The broader backdrop amplifies this move: refining margins are also widening (the news notes that oil majors' refining earnings have surged as fuel supplies tightened), and talks between Qatari mediators and Iran suggest potential escalation rather than de-escalation in the near term, keeping energy supplies tight. Tankers continue moving crude through the Strait of Hormuz despite attacks, but elevated freight rates and geopolitical risk are keeping oil prices elevated — exactly the environment that benefits crude producers.
